summary: Largely Halyard-friendly mutual NDA on counterparty paper, but with a resist-at-own-cost compelled disclosure clause, a residuals clause, a GBP 75,000 per-breach liquidated damages clause and one-way free assignment for NCL.

findings.quote: "Discloser" means the Party disclosing Confidential Information to the Recipient
findings.why: Discloser and Recipient are defined by role so either Party can be either, and the obligations apply to both.

findings.quote: which is designated as confidential or which by its nature ought reasonably to be considered confidential
findings.why: Definition covers information marked confidential or reasonably considered confidential, disclosed by either Party.

findings.quote: The Recipient shall use the Confidential Information solely for the Purpose
findings.why: Use is limited solely to the Purpose, a potential business relationship on a defined subject area.

findings.quote: The confidentiality obligations in Clause 2 do not apply to any Information that the Recipient can verify by written evidence:
findings.why: All four carve-outs (public domain, already held, third party, independently developed) are present, subject to a written-evidence standard.

findings.quote: Representative" means a director, officer, employee, external consultant, legal adviser or auditor of a Party or of any of its Affiliates.
findings.why: Advisers, auditors and Affiliates are covered on a need-to-know basis, but insurers are not listed as permitted recipients.
findings.draft_redline: "Representative" means a director, officer, employee, external consultant, legal or professional adviser, auditor or insurer of a Party or of any of its Affiliates.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Could we add insurers to the list of Representatives? Both parties may need to share information with their insurers on a confidential basis.

findings.quote: The Recipient shall, at its sole cost and expense, exhaust all legal remedies, applications and appeals to resist, stay, limit or challenge such disclosure demand before disclosing any Confidential Information
findings.why: The Receiving Party must resist and appeal at its own cost and cannot disclose without a final non-appealable order, which is far stricter than the playbook position.
findings.draft_redline: The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to the extent required by law, court, regulator or stock exchange. Where legally permitted, it shall give the Discloser prompt notice and, at the Discloser's cost, reasonably cooperate in any effort to resist or obtain confidential treatment for the disclosure.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We cannot agree to exhaust all appeals at our own cost or to wait for a final non-appealable order. We have proposed standard wording requiring notice where lawful and cooperation at the Discloser's cost.

findings.quote: provide written certification signed by an authorised officer confirming that all relevant physical and electronic files have been deleted or destroyed.
findings.why: Return or destruction with officer-signed certification, and 6.2 keeps automated backups confidential; no specific period is set but 'promptly' is not under 5 Business Days.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information remains the exclusive property of the Discloser.
findings.why: Ownership stays with the Discloser and no licence is granted other than use strictly for the Purpose.

findings.quote: Neither Party warrants the accuracy, completeness, viability or fitness for purpose of any Information shared hereunder.
findings.why: Mutual as-is disclaimer with no warranty; there is no 'no obligation to proceed' sentence.
findings.fallback_cited: Mutual disclaimers in any reasonable wording.

findings.quote: the Recipient and its personnel shall be free to use and exploit for any purpose any general ideas, concepts, know-how, skills or techniques related to the Discloser's Confidential Information that are retained in the unaided memory of the Recipient's personnel
findings.why: This is a residuals clause permitting use of information retained in unaided memory for any purpose, overriding the rest of the Agreement.
findings.draft_redline: Delete Clause 7.3 in its entirety and retitle the section 'Intellectual Property'.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to accept a residuals clause as it would undermine the protection each party relies on. We have deleted clause 7.3.

findings.quote: shall remain in effect for two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Two-year term with 30 days' notice to terminate early and three-year survival under 8.2 match the preferred position.

findings.quote: A Party shall therefore be entitled to seek injunctive relief, orders for specific performance or other interim measures
findings.why: Mutual right to seek equitable relief without proof of special damage.
findings.fallback_cited: 'Entitled to seek' rather than 'entitled to'; no requirement to post a bond.

findings.quote: the Recipient shall pay to the Discloser as liquidated damages an amount of £75,000 for each individual breach
findings.why: A fixed per-breach liquidated damages sum of GBP 75,000 is a listed deviation.
findings.draft_redline: Delete Clause 9.2. Remedies under this Agreement are cumulative and liability for breach is determined under general law.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We do not agree to fixed per-breach sums and have deleted clause 9.2. Each party remains entitled to its remedies at law and in equity.

findings.quote: except that NCL may assign or transfer this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations hereunder without consent to any Affiliate or to a corporate successor
findings.why: NCL may assign without consent while Halyard needs consent, a one-sided right.
findings.draft_redline: Either Party may assign or transfer this Agreement without consent to a member of its Group or to a successor to substantially all of its business, on written notice to the other Party. Otherwise neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have made the assignment right mutual so that both parties may assign to an Affiliate or successor on notice.

findings.quote: shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of England and Wales.
findings.why: English law governs and 10.10 gives the courts of England and Wales exclusive jurisdiction.

findings.quote: The Recipient shall not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or analyse the technical composition of any software binaries
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and hardware supplied by the Discloser is prohibited.
